name: State Water Board CIWQS Sanitary Sewer System spill data: Cat1-2-3-Spills.txt (nightly flat file)
waters_covered: statewide; all enrollees of the Sanitary Sewer Systems General Order (public systems over one mile of pipe)
access_detail: Tab-delimited text, 95 columns, ~11 MB, no auth, no bot wall on the file (the HTML map pages sit behind Incapsula). Listing page https://www.waterboards.ca.gov/water_issues/programs/sso/docs/index.php shows all files regenerated daily at about 06:00 Pacific (Last-Modified 2026-11-03 14:00 UTC). Sibling files: annualReports.txt, Enrollee_Info.txt, neworder_monthly_counts.txt, neworder_ssmps.txt, No_spill.txt, plps_spills.txt (private lateral spills), PLSD.txt. Trimmed sample: raw/ciwqs-cat1-2-3-spills-sample.json.
cadence: File rebuilt nightly. Category 1 drafts are due within 3 business days; in 2026 the median gap from spill start to SUBMIT_DRAFT_DATE was 2 days (p90 10 days, n=340). A 2026-10-30 17:00 Long Beach spill was in the 2026-11-03 file. Cal OES notified a median 4.2 hours after start (n=265). Category 3 spills arrive monthly; Category 4 only annually and are not in this file.
history: Reports under the 2022 order: start dates 2023-06-05 to 2026-10-30 (a few back to 2022). 3,708 rows: Category 1 1,382, Category 2 477, monthly Category 3 1,849. Older 2006-order spills are in other CIWQS reports (not fetched). 2026: 383 Category 1 or 2 spills to end of October.
license: No licence statement on the file listing; State Water Board public records. Quote as found: none.
legal_basis: Water Code 13263, 13267, 13383; Order WQ 2022-0103-DWQ Attachment E1
status_reason: Statewide, event-level, machine-readable, public: read hourly by pipeline/ingest/ca_swrcb_ciwqs_spills.py (If-Modified-Since: the file changes once a day; 3,567 spills since June 2023 on 2026-11-04 with the backfill: 1,284 Category 1 shown, 459 Category 2 and 1,824 Category 3 kept as reaching no water). Narrative and certifier columns never read.
notes: Drafts (Work In Progress, Draft Submitted) appear with empty receiving water and end time; they fill on certification (15 days). 141 rows of 3,708 share SPILL_EVENT_ID with another row (amended versions): key on SPILL_EVENT_ID and keep the highest SPILL_REPORT_VERSION. Date formats differ by column (MM/DD/YYYY HH:MM vs DD-MON-YY). CSO discharges from San Francisco and Sacramento are NOT in this file (they are NPDES permit events).

name: Statewide Sanitary Sewer Systems General Order WQ 2022-0103-DWQ (effective 2023-06-05), Attachment E1
status_reason: Defines categories and deadlines: Cat 1 = any volume reaching surface water; Cat 2 >= 1,000 gal not reaching water; Cat 3 50 to 999 gal; Cat 4 < 50 gal.
notes: E1 1.1: 'the Enrollee shall notify the California Office of Emergency Services and obtain a California Office of Emergency Services Control Number as soon as possible but no later than two (2) hours after: The Enrollee has knowledge of the spill' (applies to spills of 1,000 gallons or more to waters of the State). E1 3.1.1: 'Within three (3) business days of the Enrollee's knowledge of a Category 1 spill, the Enrollee shall submit a Draft Spill Report to the online CIWQS Sanitary Sewer System Database.' Certified report within 15 calendar days of spill end; technical report within 45 days for 50,000 gallons or more. The order itself imposes no public-notice duty on the enrollee; public notice falls to local health officers.

name: Health and Safety Code 5411.5 (notice to local health officer)
access_detail: leginfo returned 403 (Cloudflare challenge) to WebFetch and curl; text read from the california.public.law mirror (raw/hsc5411.5.html), which cites leginfo, current as of 2014-01-01.
status_reason: Duty to tell the health officer, not the public.
notes: (a) '... shall, as soon as that person has knowledge of the discharge, immediately notify the local health officer or the director of environmental health of the discharge.' (c) exempts discharges in compliance with waste discharge requirements.

name: Health and Safety Code 115885 and 17 CCR 7956-7961 (AB 411 beach posting and closure)
status_reason: The public duty in California: the health officer posts and closes beaches after a known sewage release and runs a closure hotline.
notes: HSC 115885(a)(1)(D): 'Establish a telephone hotline to inform the public of all beaches currently closed, posted, or otherwise restricted.' (F): 'In the event of a known untreated sewage release, immediately test the waters adjacent to the public beach and to take action pursuant to regu[lations]'. 17 CCR (quoted by a regional board document, search_only): the health officer shall '(1) Immediately post and close the beach or a portion thereof, or otherwise restrict its use until the source of the sewage release is eliminated.' Applies to ocean beaches visited by more than 50,000 people a year (AB 411).

name: Water Code 13271 and 23 CCR 2250 (Cal OES notification, 1,000 gallons)

name: SFPUC San Francisco Beach Water Quality map (combined sewer discharge flags) and getBeaches service
waters_covered: 17 San Francisco beach stations: Ocean Beach, Baker, China, Crissy Field, Aquatic Park, Mission Creek, Islais Creek, Candlestick, Crane Cove
access_detail: The map calls https://infrastructure.sfwater.org/lims.asmx/getBeaches (no auth): a JSON array wrapped in an XML <string>. Each station has stationid, stationname, cso, s_color, posted, p_color, sample_date, lat, lon. When cso is not null the map shows 'Combined Sewer Discharge has occurred within the last 24-72 hours.' Also getStation and getCSV. Saved raw/sfpuc-getBeaches.txt (all cso null on 2026-11-03).
cadence: Current state; 'We also post signs whenever a Combined Sewer System discharge occurs that affects a recreational beach' and postings stay 'until the discharge ceases' with daily sampling. Email alerts offered (no sign-up link found); hotline 1-877-SFBEACH.
history: None in the service; bacteria results on data.sf.gov v3fv-x3ux (Public Domain Dedication, rows updated 2026-11-03).
license: none stated for the service; data.sf.gov dataset ODC-PDDL
legal_basis: NPDES CA0037664 / CA0037681 CSO public notification (Nine Minimum Controls)
status_reason: Read hourly by pipeline/ingest/ca_sfpuc_beaches.py as a snapshot: the combined sewer discharge sign per station (SFPUC's own 24-72 hour window, red while shown) and the postings (beach advisories). 20 stations, no flag on 2026-11-04.
notes: Undocumented ASMX endpoint: may change without notice.

name: City of Sacramento Combined Wastewater Collection and Treatment System, Order R5-2026-0003 (NPDES CA0079111)
operator: Central Valley Regional Water Quality Control Board
status_reason: Read the public notification clause.
notes: VI.C 'viii. Notify the Public of Outflows and CSOs (a) The Discharger shall implement its "Spill Emergency Response Plan" for CSS outflow notifications and the "Combined Wastewater Collection and Treatment System Plan of Operations" for CSO notifications to ensure that the public is receiving adequate notification of CSS outflows and CSO's in accordance with the U.S. EPA's CSO Control Policy.'
